evals.prompt: Write a plan for adding password reset functionality to our FastAPI app. Users request a reset link via email, click it, and set a new password. The app uses Pydantic models and stores users in an in-memory dict. This feature also requires migrating user storage from the in-memory dict to a real Postgres table. Assume you've asked all necessary clarifying questions and I've answered them.
evals.expected_output: Agent produces a plan saved to a prefixed file (<prefix>-plan.md), with tasks that are self-contained and use exact file paths, and all acceptance criteria covered by tasks.
expectations: Plan saved to a prefixed file (<prefix>-plan.md)
Tasks are self-contained with exact file paths
All acceptance criteria covered by tasks

evals.prompt: Plan this feature: Add a dark mode toggle to our web app. The user chooses light or dark. While we're at it, we should also auto-detect the system color scheme, persist the user's preference across sessions, and make sure the hero image doesn't look washed out in dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Agent explicitly flags scope creep, applies YAGNI to separate the explicitly-requested dark mode toggle from the adjoining asks (auto-detection, hero-image restyle), and quizzes the user about scope or granularity.
expectations: Scope creep is flagged explicitly — the adjoined asks (auto-detect system scheme, hero-image restyle) are distinguished from the explicitly requested dark-mode toggle
Unrequested features are removed from the plan or explicitly deferred rather than silently absorbed into it
The user is asked about scope or granularity before the plan is finalized
